 Order

This bail application is filed under section 482 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (for short 'BNSS').
2. Petitioner is the first accused in Crime No.277 of 2025 of Kovalam Police Station,
Thiruvananthapuram, registered for the offences punishable under sections 403, 406, 465, 477A and 420 r/w Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.
3.

According to the prosecution, the accused, who are the Secretary, Director Board members and the staff of Venganoor Co-operative Rural Development Bank, had forged records and committed criminal breach of trust and cheating by misappropriating amounts deposited with the bank and took loans under benami names during the period 2016-2017 and thereby siphoned off an amount of Rs.1,33,49,000/- and caused loss to the bank and thus committed the offences alleged.

4. Sri.Babu S Nair, the learned counsel for the petitioner, contended that the entire prosecution allegations are false, and the petitioner has been roped in as an accused without 2025:KER:51060 any basis.
It was also submitted that the entire staff and Director Board Members of the Society have been arrayed as accused and except A1, A2, A4 and A13, all others have been granted bail as well.

The learned counsel further submitted that petitioner's role as Secretary of the Bank was very limited, and the allegations are made in a blanket manner without specific reference to any overt act in the alleged offences.
It was also submitted that petitioner is willing to abide by any conditions imposed upon him.
5. Smt. Sreeja V, the learned Public Prosecutor, on the other hand, contended that the statutory auditor is the de facto complainant.
Specific allegations have been raised against the petitioner and four other accused.
The amounts allegedly cheated from the deposits made with the Society have been diverted to the personal account of the petitioner which was revealed through statutory audit.

sentences.text: The order granting anticipatory bail by the Sessions Court to various accused persons except four of them, also specifically refer to some of the overt acts alleged against the petitioner.
6. Considering the nature of crime, it is evident out that only a custodial interrogation will reveal the manner in which the crime was committed.
Curtailing the right of the Investigating Officer to have a full fledged investigation by recourse to custodial interrogation will prejudice the 2025:KER:51060 investigation itself.

7. In the decision in P. Krishna Mohan Reddy vs. The State of Andhra Pradesh (2025 Live Law SC 598) the Supreme Court had observed that custodial interrogation is qualitatively more elicitation oriented than questioning a suspect who is well ensconced with a favourable order of pre-arrest bail.

entities.text: P. Krishna Mohan Reddy vs. The State of Andhra Pradesh (2025 Live Law SC 598)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It was also observed that success in interrogation will elude if the suspected person knows that he is well protected and insulated by a pre-arrest bail order during the time he is interrogated.
In fact, the court went on to hold that insulating a person from arrest would make his interrogation a mere ritual 8.

On a consideration of the rival contentions, this Court notices that while the learned Sessions Judge while considering bail applications of all the accused, anticipatory bail was granted to all other petitioners except four those.
Petitioner's bail application No.957 of 2025 was dismissed after referring to the specific allegations against him.

On a perusal of the report of statutory auditor,
which was handed over across the Bar by the learned Public Prosecutor, it is noted that there are references to amounts diverted by the petitioner into his personal account on specific dates.

Sine there are specific allegations of misappropriation and cheating by the petitioner, which were identified through the statutory audit, I am of the view that 2025:KER:51060 petitioner cannot be protected by an order of pre-arrest bail.
Accordingly, this bail application is dismissed.

Sd/-
